question: In a right-angle triangle ABC, right angled at B, AB = 8 cm. A line AO is drawn which meets BC at O such that AO = OC = 10 cm. Find the area of triangle ABC.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Recognize the common Pythagorean triplet (6, 8, 10) in right-angled ΔABO.

Given AB = 8 cm and hypotenuse AO = 10 cm, the base BO is directly 6 cm.

Since OC = 10 cm, the total base of ΔABC is BC = BO + OC = 6 + 10 = 16 cm.

Area of ΔABC = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 16 × 8 = 64 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 64 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Triangle ABC is right-angled at B.

Perpendicular side AB = 8 cm.

Line segment AO = 10 cm and OC = 10 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

Area of a Right-Angled Triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height

**Calculations:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔABO, applying the Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ AO² = AB² + BO²

⇒ 10² = 8² + BO²

⇒ 100 = 64 + BO²

⇒ BO² = 100 − 64 = 36

⇒ BO = √36 = 6 cm

⇒ Total base BC = BO + OC = 6 cm + 10 cm = 16 cm

⇒ Area of ΔABC = 1/2 × Base × Height

⇒ Area of ΔABC = 1/2 × BC × AB

⇒ Area of ΔABC = 1/2 × 16 × 8 = 64 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 64 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is strictly equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: H² = P² + B².

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of three positive integers that perfectly satisfy the Pythagoras theorem. Common exam triplets include (3, 4, 5), (6, 8, 10), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

Area of Triangle

For a triangle with a known base length and perpendicular height directly dropping to it, the area is calculated using the standard formula: Area = 1/2 × Base × Height.
